# RFID Hardware Import - user guide

## What it is for

Most installations are built from the top down: the hardware is added, the
access control module sets it up, and the people, cards and access groups are
entered afterwards. This module does the opposite. It looks at a system that
is already working - set up by another server or by hand - and writes down
what it finds: the modules, the controllers, every card and the doors it
opens. Nothing on the devices is changed. When the survey is complete, you
name the card holders, review the access groups the survey proposes, and
import everything into this system.

The survey only reads. Every command it sends is a read command, checked
against a fixed list before it leaves, and every command is logged with its
reply. The import creates records here without sending anything to the
hardware. Handing a module over to this server is a separate button that you
press on purpose.

## Where to find it

RFID System > Hardware Manager > **Import from Hardware**. The list shows the
surveys made so far; New starts one.

## The steps

1. **Modules.** Press *Find modules on the network* to search the local
   network. A module behind a router does not answer the search - add it
   with *Add a module by address*. Each module shows whether it is new here
   or already registered, how many controllers it sees and which server it
   reports to today. Tick the modules to read.
2. **Reading.** Press *Read the controllers*. The survey reads the settings
   and the whole card table of every controller, in the background; the
   page shows how far it has got and you can close it. Vending machine
   controllers are listed but never read for cards. Other kinds of devices
   (fire panels, temperature or relay controllers) are read for their
   settings only. A controller or module that could not be read is marked
   as such in the *Findings* and is not tried again on its own; once the
   cause is fixed, *Read the failed ones again* reads only those, and the
   analysis is redone - your decisions on conflicts, your choice of
   controller per schedule slot and the names you gave to groups whose cards
   did not change are kept. A module that requires a password gets it on its
   own form (*Access to the module*), then *Check again*. Press *Refresh*
   while the survey works to see how far it has got.
3. **Names.** Upload a CSV or Excel file with two columns, the person's name
   and the card number, or continue without one. Cards are matched by
   number. The same name on several lines becomes one person with several
   cards and is marked for review; *Split* turns it back into one person
   per card. Cards without a name get a generated owner named after the
   card number.
4. **Access groups.** The survey proposes access groups from the rights the
   controllers hold: doors that always go together form one group, and a
   card belongs to every group it holds. Rename the groups, or press
   *Merge groups...* to make several one; the dialog says what every card
   gains, and refuses a merge the access control module could not hold
   (the same door on different terms, or a card reaching a door through two
   groups). The *Schedules* tab shows the time schedule
   slots; where controllers disagree on a slot, choose which controller to
   take it from. The *Findings* tab lists conflicts with records already
   present here - decide for each whether to use the existing record or
   leave the surveyed one out.
5. **Import.** Press *Import...*, choose what to include (every part can be
   left out) and start it. The import runs in the background. A survey that
   stops on a problem keeps everything it read and imported so far; *Reopen
   the survey* takes it back to the step it was at, and a second start
   creates nothing twice.
6. **Hand over.** When you are ready for a module to report to this
   server, press *Point to this server* on the module, then *Enable here*.
   Until then the module keeps working with its current server.

## What to expect

* Imported modules are created switched off. Controllers come with their
  doors and readers, exactly as the access control module would build them.
* Each card opens the same doors here as it does on the controller, with the
  same schedule and the same alarm right. A person with several cards will
  open, with each card, the union of what the cards open today; such people
  are marked for review before the import.
* A right the system cannot hold exactly (a card accepted on one reader of a
  door only, or with different schedules on the two readers) is imported as
  a right on the whole door and noted in the report.
* A second survey of the same site creates nothing twice.
* The report lists everything that was created, left out or could not be
  represented exactly, and can be downloaded as a text file.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does the survey change anything on the controllers?** No. It only reads,
and the command log on the survey shows every command it sent.

**Can I read a module that reports to another server?** Yes. The survey
talks to the module directly and does not change where it reports to.

**A controller is listed as "Not reachable" or "Failed".** The module or the
controller did not answer, or answered with a damaged reply. Check the
device and press *Check again* on the module, or start a new survey.

**Why is a vending machine controller left out?** Vending machines hold a
product and price table, not access rights; they are not part of an access
control import.
